site.title: AzraelGodKing — RimWorld Mods
site.tagline: RimWorld mods for colonies that farm, harden, dig, remember, make time for each other, and keep the small comforts.
site.heroIntro: Seven mods. One workshop. Open a mod page for details — or jump straight to Steam or zip downloads if you cannot use the Workshop. Every mod ships as a GitHub release zip; extract into your RimWorld Mods folder. All mods need Harmony.
site.author: AzraelGodKing

mods.name: Homesteader
mods.tagline: Farm-to-table craft, wells and irrigation, cool cellars, and off-grid power for tribal and homestead starts.
overview: Grow it, put it by, live off the land. Homesteader brings tribal survival, farm-to-table crafting, wells and irrigation, cool storage, comforts, and off-grid power to colonies far from the glitterworld supply chain.
The Homesteaders scenario starts three settlers with livestock and hand tools. A homestead supplier caravan visits with preserves, seeds, and the occasional Diggo plushie.

features.title: Preserve without a freezer
features.body: Dry, salt, and smoke from day one of a tribal start. The drying rack needs no research; curing and smoking unlock with Primitive homestead. Turn surplus into stores that survive the caravan and the cold snap.

features.title: Drying rack
features.body: No research. Jerky, fruit leather, dried produce, dried mushrooms, and pemmican.

features.title: Curing rack
features.body: Primitive homestead. Rock salt and salted meat — not the same job as drying.

features.title: Smokehouse
features.body: Smoked meat — and smoked fish with Odyssey.

features.title: Bulk farm storage
features.body: Hayloft and ingredient barrel for bulk farm storage.

features.title: A kitchen that earns its keep
features.body: Mill grain, churn butter, press cheese, brew cider, and plate pantry meals at the homestead hearth. Recipes lean on what you grew — cream, sugar, fruit, and smoked leftovers — not a chemfuel factory.

features.title: Workstations
features.body: Grain mill, butter churn, cheese press, pickling crock, jam cauldron, and brewing bench.

features.title: Hearth meals
features.body: Toast and jam, ploughman's lunch, honey porridge, and pie. The homestead hearth cooks; the wood stove only heats.

features.title: Favorite foods
features.body: Pawns remember what they love.

features.title: Water that feeds the fields
features.body: Former Wellspring content ships inside Homesteader. Draw, catch, store, and trench water into irrigated soil.

features.title: Wells and barrels
features.body: Hand-dug and deep wells, rain barrel, cistern, and solar still.

features.title: Irrigation
features.body: Irrigated soil and planter for reliable crops.

features.title: Wellcraft goods
features.body: Boiled water, mud bricks, and clean bandages.

features.title: Plumbing bridge
features.body: With Dubs Bad Hygiene, tanks join the plumbing net — an optional Bad Hygiene plumbing bridge.

features.title: Power without the glitterworld
features.body: Compact batteries and wood-fired generators keep a homestead lit when the grid fails.

features.title: Batteries
features.body: Compact, bank, advanced, and ultratech cells for tight footprints.

features.title: Generators
features.body: Chemfuel portable and wood-burning options for rural power.

features.title: Primitive homestead
features.body: Unlocks curing, smoking, and dairy.

features.title: Advanced homestead
features.body: Unlocks the wood-burning generator.

features.title: Wellcraft / Irrigation / Waterworks
features.body: Unlock wells and irrigated land.

features.title: Start here
features.body: Three settlers, livestock, and hand tools — far from the glitterworld supply chain. A homestead supplier caravan visits with preserves, seeds, and the occasional Diggo plushie.

stationFaq.title: Which station do I want?
stationFaq.intro: Similar names, different jobs — nothing here is a duplicate.

rows.answer: Drying rack needs no research: jerky, dried produce, fruit leather, dried mushrooms, pemmican. Curing rack (Primitive homestead) salts meat and chips rock salt.

rows.pair: Root cellar vs icehouse vs springhouse
rows.answer: Root cellar is the large passive larder (≤5°C). Icehouse is colder and smaller (≤0°C). Springhouse is milder (≤8°C) for dairy and produce by the farmhouse.
Homestead hearth cooks pantry meals. Wood stove only heats the room, off-grid — it does not cook.

goodToKnow: The drying rack needs no research. Curing and smoking unlock with Primitive homestead.
Smoked fish requires the Odyssey DLC.
Safe to add to an existing save. Before removing, deconstruct Homesteader buildings and use up or sell its items.

compatibleWith.note: Optional plumbing bridge — water tanks join the plumbing net

compatibleWith.name: Stormproof
compatibleWith.note: Pairs naturally — Stormproof grid defense runs on Homesteader batteries and generators

mods.name: Stormproof
mods.tagline: Defend the power grid from flares, lightning, short circuits, EMP, and fallout — then call the storm yourself.
overview: Natural disasters. Grid defense. Hazard hardening. Custom C# components patch vanilla events to keep your power grid running through everything the Rim throws at it.
Seventeen tools for a disaster-hardened colony — plus one purely decorative weather vane. Pairs naturally with Homesteader batteries and generators.

features.title: Storm spire
features.body: Attracts lightning strikes within a 30-tile radius, keeping fires away from your base. It cannot burn and snuffs out flames a caught strike sparks around its base. Grid-connected, each strike dumps up to 1,500 Wd into your capacitors and batteries — with a 5% chance of a "Zzzt!" surge, eliminated entirely by perfect grounding research.

features.title: Surge protector
features.body: Absorbs one "Zzzt!" short circuit, then needs a day to recharge and takes internal damage. Pairs dangerously well with a grid-connected storm spire.

features.title: Armored conduit
features.body: Power conduit sheathed in riveted steel. Fireproof and far tougher than standard conduit — the wiring of choice for killboxes and exterior walls.

features.title: Storm capacitor bank
features.body: A lightning-only battery. The grid can't charge it — only spire-caught strikes can — but it never self-discharges and "Zzzt!" surges can't drain it. When grid production falls short it automatically discharges up to 2,000W to cover the deficit.

features.title: Load shedder
features.body: An automatic breaker between the main grid and a low-priority sub-grid. Transmits like a conduit while supply batteries hold charge; trips open and sheds the sub-grid when they fall below the cutoff (default 20%), then reconnects once they recover.

features.title: Grid monitor console
features.body: Live production, consumption, battery charge, and time until the batteries run dry (or fill up) in its inspect panel. Warns at 25% stored charge, sounds the alarm at 10%.

features.title: Weather forecaster
features.body: Shows how long the current weather will hold, announces incoming thunderstorms so you can ready your spires, and warns you an hour before the weather breaks.

features.title: Solar shield
features.body: A field generator that keeps every electrical device on the map running during a solar flare by drawing 2,500W continuously. Stockpile battery charge before the sky goes red — if the grid runs dry mid-flare, the shield collapses and everything stays dark until the flare ends.

features.title: EMP dampener
features.body: Colony buildings in a ~15-tile radius shrug off EMP stuns. Turrets keep firing through EMP mortar barrages. Does not protect pawns or mechanoids.

features.title: Static discharge pylon
features.body: Runs exclusively on bottled lightning: every shock drains 50 Wd from a storm capacitor bank on its power net, repeatedly stunning and burning raiders and mechanoids in its radius. No capacitor charge, no zap.

features.title: Fallout scrubber
features.body: Strips airborne toxins from an enclosed room. Pawns and animals inside slowly shed toxic buildup, faster than serious fallout adds it.

features.title: Atmospheric barrier
features.body: Map-wide toxin hardener. Suppresses toxic fallout, toxic surge, volcanic ash, and noxious haze while the grid holds charge. Pair with fallout scrubbers to clear buildup already in the blood.

features.title: Climate stabilizer
features.body: Cancels temperature offsets from heat waves, cold snaps, volcanic winters, heat domes, and polar fronts — as long as batteries can feed it.

features.title: Sky restorer
features.body: Restores usable daylight during eclipses, volcanic winters and ash, and darkened skies so crops and colonists aren't stuck in permanent dusk.

features.title: Fire suppressor
features.body: Extinguishes fires in a ~25-tile radius while powered. Pairs with storm spires during flashstorms and dry lightning fronts.

features.title: Drought condenser
features.body: Cancels drought plant-growth penalties map-wide while powered. Most useful with Odyssey grasslands droughts.

features.title: Storm caller
features.body: An ionospheric agitator that summons a rainy thunderstorm on demand: lightning to feed your storm spires, rain to douse wildfires. Half-day storm, five-day recharge — a supplement to your grid, not a replacement for it.

features.title: Storm vane
features.body: A handsome copper weather vane. It doesn't predict anything, prevent anything, or power anything. But every proper homestead has one.

features.title: Ion storm
features.body: A new small-threat event (0.75-1.5 days): batteries bleed ~20% of stored charge per day, random EMP bursts pop at powered buildings, and extra "Zzzt!" surges fire. EMP dampeners, surge protectors, and storm capacitor banks are the counters.

features.title: More events to earn the kit
features.body: Heat dome, polar front, toxic surge, and dry lightning front each pressure a different counter. Vanilla fallout, heat/cold, eclipse, volcanic winter, flashstorm, and drought are covered too once hazard hardening is online.

features.title: Solar flare bypass
features.body: While active, the solar shield patches the global electricity-disabled flag so your colony keeps running — as long as the grid can feed 2,500W.

features.title: Lightning harvesting
features.body: The storm spire intercepts lightning strikes in range and sweeps its base clear of fire after each hit. Wired spires charge capacitors first, then batteries; unwired spires simply ground the bolt safely.

features.title: Weather awareness
features.body: The forecaster reads the map's weather engine directly — its inspect panel shows exactly how long the current weather will last, and it pings you when storms roll in or the weather is about to break.

features.title: EMP immunity
features.body: The EMP dampener patches building stun logic so turrets, doors, and production buildings inside its radius ignore EMP effects.

features.title: Automatic load shedding
features.body: The load shedder watches its supply grid's battery charge and rewires the power net on the fly — shedding the sub-grid below the cutoff, reconnecting once charge recovers past a hysteresis margin so it never chatters.

features.title: Natural hazard hardening
features.body: Late-game buildings cancel toxic fallout, extreme heat/cold, eclipses, flashstorm fires, and drought growth penalties while they have grid power — the same solar-shield fantasy applied to most natural incidents.

goodToKnow: Stockpile battery charge before the sky goes red — if the grid runs dry mid-flare, the solar shield collapses and everything stays dark until the flare ends.
A grid-connected storm spire has a 5% chance per caught strike of triggering a "Zzzt!" surge; perfect grounding research eliminates it entirely.
Storm capacitor banks are lightning-only — the grid cannot charge them, and spires fill capacitors before regular batteries.
Load Stormproof after Harmony in your mod list.
Safe to add mid-save. Deconstruct all Stormproof buildings before removing the mod.

compatibleWith.name: Homesteader
compatibleWith.note: Pairs naturally with Homesteader batteries and generators

compatibleWith.note: Nemesis EMP sabotage respects EMP dampeners; surge protectors blunt its grid sabotage

mods.name: Strata
mods.tagline: Dig down, build up, breathe deep. Multistory bases with commuting colonists and Odyssey-ready stacks.
overview: One home, many floors. Carve rock under your colony, frame a roof deck above it, and treat every floor as one settlement. Colonists commute for work, food, rest, hauling, medicine, and rituals. Power, smoke, and (optionally) pipes follow the shafts with them.
V3 hardens that column — see-through decks, cross-level combat and construction, and Odyssey gravship stacks that actually stay linked through launch and land.
Odyssey unlocks gravship stairwells and ship stacks only — dig, tower decks, atmosphere, and colony logistics work without the DLC. Default level cap is ±2 (Unlimited off).

features.title: See-below roof decks
features.body: Look through open sky and see-through roof deck into the map below — terrain, buildings, live pawns and projectiles. Click-select, double-click select-similar, forbidden overlays, and float menus work on what you can see. A+ weather syncs from the floor underneath.

features.title: Cross-level combat
features.body: Pawns, turrets, and mortars can fire through open shafts and sky holes. Auto-engage keeps decks and underfloors in the fight without hopping maps by hand.

features.title: Force-build across floors
features.body: Prioritize or construct when steel or wood only exists on another linked stockpile. Pawns walk the stairs, haul, and deliver — including Ideology gates and turret history. Work relay defaults on.

features.title: One inventory column
features.body: Combined resources (default on) sum linked stockpiles for the readout and build menu. Install minified buildings onto blueprints on other floors. Medical beds and rest can pin across the stack.

features.title: Gravship stacks
features.body: Ship-only stairwells open A+/B+ pockets that travel on launch and reattach on landing. Stable shaft IDs, travel entitlement toggle, cargo pack/place, land polish, and pilot the ship from a linked underdeck.

features.title: Living colony polish
features.body: Mental breaks and raiders chase through shafts. Visitors use stairs. Depth-dim slider for upper decks. Fault guards auto-kill broken subsystems. Native cavern biome when Biomes! Caverns is absent.

features.title: Dig down
features.body: Research digging down, build an excavated stairwell, open a full-size rock level under your map. Deeper floors need deep excavation. Second shafts join the same level.

features.title: Build up
features.body: Research building up, frame a tower stairwell, open outdoor Level +N as a roof deck — walk and build where the floor below is roofed. Expand roofs downstairs to grow the deck.

features.title: One colony column
features.body: Work, food, rest, medical, joy, schedule, storage priority, construction pull, ritual escorts, caravan pull, raid pursuit — across every linked floor.

features.title: Atmosphere
features.body: Smoke, deep gas, O₂, and CO₂ share one sim (optional; gases default off for performance). Vent, pipe, or exchange through shafts. Overlay in play settings. Performance mode and vacant-level throttle keep tall colonies playable.

features.title: Living below
features.body: Shoring, gas airlocks, ore hoists, fungus farms, sump pumps, mine lamps, bellows, lime scrubbers — plus a deep-gas well and smokeless generator.

features.title: Excavated / tower stairwell
features.body: Opens B− or A+. Ties power when wired. Seal to stop gas and raiders. Elevators do the same in 1×1 with a power gate on the paid direction.

features.title: Shaft power conduit
features.body: Optional dedicated tie away from the stair footprint — builds its partner below automatically. Tankless pockets still wake from shaft surplus.

features.title: Ventilation kit
features.body: Smoke hole (no research), louvers, exhaust fans, updraft filters, gas pipes. A working outlet keeps a room under harmful smoke.

features.title: Life support
features.body: O₂ / CO₂ pumps, shaft exchangers, canary cages. Medieval bellows and lime scrubbers if you're not industrial yet. Gravship O₂ reclaimers and tanks when Odyssey is loaded.

features.title: Elevators
features.body: Compact powered shafts for the same dig / tower / gravship roles as stairwells — faster transit, smaller footprint.

features.title: Deep gas & wells
features.body: Cap a vent, burn canisters in the deep-gas generator, or feed Helixien pipes when Vanilla Helixien Gas Expanded is present.

features.title: Away into the dark
features.body: World sites: sunken ruins, collapsed mines, sealed vaults, geothermal vents.

features.title: At home
features.body: Cave breakthroughs, gas firestorms, flood seeps, rich ore nodes, optional ancient stairwells.

features.title: Fluid shafts
features.body: Soft-dep junctions for Dubs Bad Hygiene, Dubs Central Heating, Rimatomics, Vanilla Helixien Gas Expanded, Rimefeller, and VEF chemfuel — meter across levels without merging pipe nets.

features.title: Modder API & soft-compat
features.body: Strata.StrataModderApi for reachable maps and link listeners. Soft bridges for Vehicle Framework roof decks, VGE Chapter 1, ReGrowth underdecks, and sister mods in this series. Cave mods (Deep And Deeper, Anomaly undercaves) stay invisible to Strata's relays by default — an opt-in setting extends relays into their caves.

features.title: Own Strata tab
features.body: Medieval opens floors; industrial keeps them livable.

features.title: Building up
features.body: Unlocks the tower stairwell and Level A+.

features.title: Digging down
features.body: Opens B1; Deep excavation opens B2+ and quest sites.

features.title: Electricity branch
features.body: Elevators and Shaft power, then Fluid shafts.

features.title: Forced ventilation
features.body: Leads to Deep life support and Deep gas extraction.

features.title: Support techs
features.body: Rock shoring, Passive life support, Deep infrastructure, Deep agriculture, Mine atmosphere.

goodToKnow: Leave pillars under thick rock roof — or research shoring.
Seal a shaft to stop raiders and gas; it also traps your own people.
Grow A+ by expanding roofs downstairs; open sky never holds buildings, but you can see and shoot through it.
On Odyssey ships, only gravship stairwells place on the footprint; dig/tower stairs stay planet-side.
Prefer a smaller map size if you plan many deep floors — each level is a full same-size map.
Leave Natural / Pollutant gases off unless you want the atmosphere sim; use Performance mode to A/B lag.
Safe to add mid-save. Before removing: bring everyone up, haul what you care about, deconstruct all stairwells (Abandon confirm if a linked level still has colony presence).

Mods adding fuel-burning buildings are not auto-tagged by heuristic; only a named vanilla/DLC list plus XML patches get smoke comps.
Multi-level mods that patch pathfinding or map generation globally are the most likely source of conflicts; Strata deliberately patches neither.

mods.name: Nemesis
mods.tagline: A named antagonist who taunts, sabotages, and returns with an army — until you end the hunt.
overview: Someone remembers. Someone is coming back. A named pawn from a hostile faction becomes a personal antagonist — not another faceless raid. Early on they harass with taunts, false leads, and sabotage. After each escape they level up as a combat captain (skills, gear, armor) and prefer returning with an army. The hunt still ends when you capture or kill them… or when they get what they came for.
Original design and core runtime by Dredd (Misakabob). Expanded and packaged here by AzraelGodKing with gratitude.

features.title: Killed ally or kin
features.body: A colonist kills someone's ally or kin. Someone takes it personally.

features.title: Prison break / slave escape
features.body: A prisoner (or Ideology slave) breaks out — and a former friend of the colony does not forgive it.

features.title: Wounded escape
features.body: An enemy is wounded, escapes the map, then comes back for the colonist who cut them.

features.title: Fixation
features.body: An enemy who killed one of yours fixates on a surviving colonist and makes it personal.

features.title: Taunts & notes
features.body: Comms taunts and paper notes that name your people. Soft-compat lines can reference Homesteader cellars / favorites and Stormproof ion flavor when those mods are loaded.

features.title: Raids & vengeance army
features.body: Faction raids — and after escapes, vengeance army returns that inject the same nemesis into a heavier assault. Why return alone when you can return with an army? Raid points also scale with captain level.

features.title: Captain progression
features.body: Each escape raises captain level: combat focus (Destroyer, Berserker, Sniper, Psycho, Survivor, Mechanitor), better skills and gear, battle-hardened armor. Biotech can add bionics/genes. Soft animal escorts and Mechanitor mech retinues when those systems are present. Still killable after enough escapes — no cheat-death.

features.title: Personal assault
features.body: On-map assaults that pull back when losing. They heal between escapes so the hunt keeps coming.

features.title: False signals
features.body: Fake distress / trader offers that become delayed ambushes (downweighted after escapes).

features.title: Sabotage & waste
features.body: EMP / grid sabotage, Biotech waste drops, caravan harassment, and food-store vandalism — common early; less likely once they start returning as a captain.

features.title: Anomaly bait
features.body: Optional Anomaly baiting when that DLC is active (fail-open without it).

features.title: Capture
features.body: Arrest them alive, then Execute / Release / Keep / Truce from the resolution dialog.

features.title: Corner & kill
features.body: After enough escapes they can finally be finished for good.

features.title: They win
features.body: If they hunt a specific colonist, the hunt also ends if that pawn dies or is handed over — they get what they came for.

goodToKnow: Trigger chances, aggression pacing, and the action mix are configurable in mod settings.
No cheat-death — the nemesis is still killable after enough escapes.
Safe to add mid-save; resolve any active hunt before removing the mod.

mods.name: Deep Colony
mods.tagline: Perks, trauma & therapy, apprenticeship, inheritance, and a living faction reputation ledger.
overview: Your colonists are more than their stats. Five interlocking systems give each colonist a real identity — and make your colony feel like it has a living history. Not more furniture. Not another raid timer.
Inspect panels show perk points, mentor / apprentices, and active trauma.

features.title: Three colony tabs
features.body: See every colonist's perks and unspent points, trace founder bloodlines and teaching lineages, and read the full goodwill ledger per faction.

features.title: Mod settings & presets
features.body: Every system has its own toggle, plus sliders for combat shock, mentor XP, drift pacing, inheritance, and therapy strength.

features.title: Power tier (opt-in)
features.body: Skill-20 capstones, branching level-15 picks, respec, cross-skill archetypes, chronic trauma, and attitude-driven consequences.

features.title: Perk points
features.body: At skill levels 5 and 15, colonists earn perk points for permanent passive bonuses. Every skill has its own tree, with exact numbers in the tooltips.

features.title: Combat & medicine
features.body: Practiced eye to crack shot. Brawler's instinct to battle hardened. First aid mastery to surgeon's touch.

features.title: Craft & colony
features.body: Construction, Crafting, Plants, Animals, Mining, Intellectual, Social, Cooking, and Artistic — each with its own path.

features.title: Muscle memory
features.body: Perks slow skill rust — and reclaiming lost levels earns double XP. Recruits who join past a gate arrive with points (or a modest pre-pick).

features.title: Capstones & branches
features.body: Skill 20 unlocks a capstone perk; level 15 becomes a branching pick. Respec at the cost of a cooldown and a bruised ego.

features.title: Cross-skill archetypes
features.body: Colonists whose perks span the right skills grow into archetypes — a named identity with its own bonus, earned from how they actually lived.

features.title: Trauma types
features.body: Combat shock, violent loss, captivity trauma, massacre survivor, and bereavement shock when grief stacks. Trauma fades over weeks.

features.title: Specialty trauma
features.body: Fire, toxic exposure, insect swarms, and betrayal each leave their own mark — and their own triggers to avoid.

features.title: Counsel
features.body: Doctors can counsel the wounded mind (workgiver or right-click). Therapy quality scales with the counselor's Social skill, opinion, and the room. Casual therapy chats still help as a light supplement.

features.title: Group counseling
features.body: One counselor, several patients — slower per pawn, but it keeps a shaken colony moving after a bad raid.

features.title: Scars & resilience
features.body: Recovery leaves something behind: sometimes a lingering scar, sometimes resilience — a colonist genuinely hardened by what they survived.

features.title: Living with it
features.body: Contextual flashbacks, combat habits shaped by old wounds, grudges against the faction responsible, and days of remembrance for the dead. Three counsel sessions forge a confidant bond that makes future therapy stronger.

features.title: Pair veteran and rookie
features.body: Pair a veteran with a rookie via right-click — pick the skill to focus on. Mentors must lead by 3+ skill levels; family only needs 2.

features.title: Passive learning
features.body: Apprentices earn bonus XP while working near their mentor.

features.title: Mentoring work
features.body: Dedicated Mentoring work type runs active teaching sessions. Multiple pairs can run at once — and a Biotech blackboard in the room boosts the XP.

features.title: Elders
features.body: Colonists past 60 slow down at labor but shine as mentors, and earn one late perk point. Your founders stay valuable to the end.

features.title: Graduation & rivalry
features.body: Graduating apprentices can pick up their mentor's first perk — and maybe a new passion. Professional rivals in the same craft push each other's XP.

features.title: Inherited traits and passions
features.body: Children and recruits with colonist parents can inherit traits and passions. Build long enough and you'll see echoes of your founders.

features.title: Deeper inheritance
features.body: Dead parents and grandparents count too, families develop skill traditions, and adoptive caregivers can echo a passion onto their wards.

features.title: Founder surnames
features.body: Colony-born children carry founder and parent surnames, so your bloodlines read like bloodlines.

features.title: Heirlooms
features.body: When a colonist dies, a treasured possession passes to their kin — a small comfort with a long memory.

features.title: Living goodwill
features.body: Raids, trades, gifts, and shared-enemy kills nudge goodwill. Strong friendships and deep enmities slowly drift over time without constant contact — allies don't collapse overnight from idle drift.

features.title: Reputation ledger
features.body: The Reputation tab shows every faction's ledger: what moved goodwill, when, and what drift is still pending.

features.title: Personal envoys
features.body: Assign a colonist as envoy to a faction for steady goodwill — but if they die, the relationship takes it personally.

features.title: Settlement epithets
features.body: Settlements earn epithets from your shared history — grudges and favors written on the world map.

goodToKnow: Soft and Default presets keep power systems and attitude consequences off; Hard enables skill-20 capstones, branching perks, chronic trauma, and attitude-driven trade / caravan / raid pressure.
The Perks tab shows every colonist's trees at a glance, and an alert nudges you when points sit unspent.
The Legacy tab traces founder lines, family traditions, and who taught whom.
On the Hard preset, trauma left untreated until it expires can settle into chronic stress — counseling eases it back down.
On the Hard preset, attitude has teeth — trade prices, caravan access, and raid pressure follow how factions actually feel about you.

compatibleWith.name: Biotech
compatibleWith.note: A blackboard in the room boosts mentoring XP

mods.name: Date Night
mods.tagline: Paint Date or Lovin on the Schedule tab. Dates are walks and tables; Lovin still uses a double.
overview: Schedule romance. Make memories. Adds Date and Lovin timetable slots to the Schedule tab. Date hours are a walk, a table, or hanging out — mood and opinion, no bed. Paint Lovin on both partners for the same hours and they meet in a shared double; lovin uses a short mean-time-between until the schedule changes.
Adults without a partner in that bed can have some private time in any bed. Children never qualify.

features.title: 1. Paint Date or Lovin
features.body: Open Schedule and pick the teal Date or rose Lovin button (vanilla hardcodes that grid, so XML alone never shows a custom slot). With Rimbody, Exosuit, or Schedule Everything, they sit in the next free extra columns so those mods keep Workout / Piloting.

features.title: 2. Date hours
features.body: Assign the same hours on both lovers. They meet at a table, gathering spot, or just walk together. Mood and opinion only — no bed, no pregnancy. Couples remember a favourite venue; two couples with overlapping Date hours may share one (double date).

features.title: 3. Lovin hours
features.body: Each paths to a shared rendezvous double (claimed for the window, then restored). When both are in it, lovin uses a short MTB. Ideology that forbids lovin, or Biotech sterile genes, reroute to a date instead. Adults without a partner in that bed can have private time. Children never qualify.

features.title: 4. Show up
features.body: If a partner is drafted, in a medical bed, or off-map for the window, the one who waited gets a short stood-up thought. If both make it, they get a small boost. Hungry, chemical desire, player-forced jobs, and exhaustion still come first. The anniversary of a love bond sends a letter — a date that day is the year's peak.

features.title: Pregnancy-safe cooldown
features.body: Only shortens lovin chance while scheduled; keeps vanilla post-lovin cooldown so pregnancy rolls stay sane.

features.title: Eager mode
features.body: Also shortens post-lovin cooldown like Always Do Lovin. Can spam pregnancy rolls — leave off unless you want that.

features.title: Allow private time
features.body: Adults on Lovin hours use any bed when a couple job cannot start. Mood thought only — no pregnancy. Same cooldown as lovin. Children never qualify.

features.title: Claim double for Lovin hours
features.body: Temporarily assign the rendezvous double to the couple, then restore their previous beds when the window ends.

features.title: Anniversaries
features.body: Letter and a small mood on the love-bond anniversary. A date that actually lands that day is a much bigger boost.

features.title: Remember favourite spots
features.body: Couples prefer the venue of their best dates. A ruined date can sour that place.

features.title: Allow double dates
features.body: Two couples with overlapping Date hours may share a venue. Quality rolls once; the evening spills into opinions of the other pair. If the other couple never shows, they date alone.

features.title: Date
features.body: Love relationship, both scheduled Date, same map — adults only.

features.title: Lovin
features.body: Both scheduled Lovin, reachable shared double (claimed for the window).

features.title: Mismatch alert
features.body: A schedule mismatch alert fires if only one lover has Date or Lovin painted.

features.title: Private time
features.body: Adult colonist, Lovin hours, any reachable bed (toggle in settings).

features.title: Ideology / Biotech
features.body: No-lovin precepts and sterile genes reroute to Date.

features.title: No-sleep pawns
features.body: Works for no-sleep / low-rest pawns who never hit a Sleep block.

goodToKnow: Safe to add mid-save. Before removing, clear Date / Lovin slots back to Sleep / Anything.
With Dev mode on, a Date Night menu can make a selected pair lovers, click-to-pair, paint Lovin or Date all day, force lovin / private time / date now, and log the rendezvous bed.
After installing, open a colonist's Schedule tab — Date and Lovin appear beside Sleep.

mods.name: Niceties
mods.tagline: Small colony comforts: well-kept apparel, throne-room altars, any outfit cut, hidden cryptosleep, melee hunting, and shared bedrooms.
overview: Vanilla never shipped these. Niceties is one Harmony QoL companion: each nicety is its own Mod Options toggle. Soft / Default / Hard only seed the knobs — they are not a forced bundle.

Combat, fire, and outdoor rot stay vanilla. Royalty and Ideology are optional; those toggles no-op without the DLC. Safe to add or remove mid-save. Inspired by older Workshop ideas, rewritten from scratch for 1.6 — not a port of those mods.

features.title: Daily wear by quality
features.body: Worn clothes skip or scale the daily deterioration tick. Quality and Crafting skill decide how often a piece loses a hit point. Masterwork and legendary stay as they are.

features.title: Combat still shreds
features.body: Combat, fire, and outdoor rot are left alone. This is wardrobe care, not invincible armor.

features.title: Corpse clothes
features.body: Optional: apparel on a corpse keeps the same daily-wear rule.

features.title: Altars allowed
features.body: Royalty throne rooms may hold an Ideology altar without failing the no-altars check.

features.title: Throne wins the room
features.body: If a throne is in the room, it stays a throne room rather than flipping to a temple.

features.title: Gender tags off
features.body: Apparel gender tags are captured at load and cleared so mixed royal cuts do not apply the wrong-gender thought.

features.title: Toggle restores tags
features.body: Turn the nicety off and the original tags come back.

features.title: Off the bar
features.body: Pawns already in a cryptosleep casket drop off the colonist bar and reappear when ejected.

features.title: Carrying in stays visible
features.body: Carrying someone to a casket does not hide them early — that crash is what broke older hide-from-bar mods.

features.title: Hunt with a melee weapon
features.body: Hunters may hunt with a melee weapon instead of only a ranged one.

features.title: Body-size cap
features.body: A prey size cap keeps people from charging a thrumbo with a knife unless you raise it.

features.title: Unarmed optional
features.body: Unarmed hunting is off by default.

features.title: Mark the room
features.body: Select a bed and toggle Share room. Every bed in that room shares the flag.

features.title: Stays a bedroom
features.body: Extra beds no longer flip the room to barracks, so Slept in bedroom and royal bedroom requirements still apply.

features.title: No disturbed sleep
features.body: Pawns who share a room — marked, or another colonist assigned a bed there — skip the disturbed-sleep thought. A private room still notices haulers walking through.

features.title: Same mattress
features.body: Sharing one bed with someone who is not a partner is still vanilla.

features.title: Independent toggles
features.body: Each nicety is its own on/off. Nested knobs (quality scaling, unarmed hunt, body-size cap) only apply while that nicety is on.

features.title: Soft
features.body: No daily clothing wear, corpse clothes included, unarmed hunting, any prey size. A starting point — not a bundle you must keep.

features.title: Default
features.body: Quality-scaled wear, melee up to body size 1.5, no unarmed.

features.title: Hard
features.body: No crafting bonus, melee only small game (0.8).

goodToKnow: Safe to add or remove mid-save.
Requires Harmony. Royalty and Ideology are optional.
Do not run alongside Jecs Everlasting Apparel, Allow Altars in Throneroom, Wear What You Want, Hide Cryptosleep Pawn, or Share Rooms [LWM] — they overlap the same jobs.
Workshop preview is an options-card collage (Homesteader straw-hat sprite + pixel icons), not a painted poster.
